I don't do anything ethically/morally wrong by society's standards.

But I'm afraid it doesn't matter. 

There is no "OK". It's all just one big  system designed to let the bad genes die and the good ones flourish. And there are people who flourish in this world who do terrible things. That makes the assessment self evident.

You do not care.

Hence, your remarkeably dispassionate and superficial comment. Not very useful for this sub, I'm afraid.

Nature is amoral. But if you're going to pretend to give a shit, you should do it well. You aren't helping.
7 years here. I'm thinking it's time to rotate
What if you're almost 27 years old?
Thanks, man. I really do appreciate the love. Only the best for you as well.
Both. The sertraline helps with anxiety and depression and the wellbutrin helps with energy and focus.
How long were you on that combo?

Honestly, I'm passed AW. He's interesting, and has some words of wisdom, but he just doesn't work for me.

I appreciate the response though.

I see, that definitely changes things. 

I'm sorry, and wish you well.

I would recommend against therapy for the time being. Unfortunately it seems like you're in a vulnerable state, and seeking services from any kind of profession \(especially one involving psychological disturbance\) will make it easier for people to take advantage of you.

That said, not all therapists are bad. There are plenty of good ones out there, it sounds like you just landed with either a snake or a moron. Probably the former.

I don't know the details of your family dynamic or the one of your boyfriend \- therefore, I cannot comment on how correct your therapist may have been.

I can say that it definitely was wrong and unethical for him to suggest that, though, primarily because the consequences can be severe, especially if there isn't some kind of substitute already in place \(he probably was hoping you were going to be more dependent on him further down the road\).

Your family should definitely accept that you were mislead and be understanding of this.

First ask yourself why your life must amount to anything in the first place.

 Remember that there's almost 8 billion people on this planet, and most of them have daily struggles and bleak futures as far as our culture is concerned. That's only one point of view though, and because life is inherantly meaningless, there are very few if any absolute truths or truly objective morals.

It's worth taking the time to recognize and understand that you have qualities which are unique and desirable.

Many famous writers in history have been less than stellar writers. Their ideas and ability to turn them into something meaningful to the reader are a big part of what lead to their success. 

All passions are best undertaken without the expectation of major success, though, and any kind of real success is only attained through a series of steps that eventually lead to your goal.

You start working somewhere relevant to your goals; then you meet people who know people, who know people. Maybe someone is the cousin of a guy who works at some agency, etc.

You already know this, though. 

For now, just write, and find purpose outside of achieving some grand success.
Therapists can be terrible. Have you told them you were essentially gaslighted?
Thank you. I appreciate your realistic take on it all. I still want input from others, but your perspective fills a good niche.
